reasoning: 1. TARGET ENGAGEMENT: No direct target engagement data reported for either PSMA (I-131-1095) or AR (enzalutamide). However, the significant PSA response in the combination arm (44% vs 10%, p=0.0025) suggests biological activity. 2. PATHWAY MODULATION: No biomarker data available to assess pathway changes. The PSA response itself serves as a downstream readout of biological activity. 3. CLINICAL TRANSLATION: Primary endpoint was met with statistically significant and clinically meaningful effect - PSA response rate 44% in combination arm vs 10% in enzalutamide monotherapy arm (p=0.0025). This represents a substantial improvement. 4. POPULATION EFFECTS: No subgroup analyses reported. The trial enrolled metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer patients who progressed on abiraterone. 5. CONFOUNDERS: The trial had adequate power and duration (53 weeks). There were notable hematologic toxicities in the combination arm including myelodysplastic syndrome (3.9% vs 0%), but these did not prevent demonstration of efficacy.
